summary: I read the case line by line and checked 57 elements against what Caplet has written. Caplet gets the cash flows, the payment-first priority and the credibility logic right. It under-answers the case's "define / explain / state / justify" asks, and it nearly ignores flexibility, "meaningful" and what the residency actually is. IPS V5 uses the case's key concepts zero times: "flexibility" (5 times in the case, 6 in the IPS brief), "responsibly" (4 and 3) and "liquidity" (1 and 4). V1 to V3 had a certainty definition and "a responsible facility contribution that leaves Laura flexibility"; V5 dropped both. "The half Laura keeps" does three jobs in V5: first cover for payment shortfalls, a cushion for costs and co-sponsor gaps, and the defence against inflation and the Taiwan dollar. Across the repo it is invested three different ways (equity in V5, T-bills in ips_spec, Treasuries to 2042 in D6). In a 1-in-20 bad market it is only about $15-17k (MODEL), below the team's own cited $25k reserve benchmark. The operating-reserve and certainty ask has six explicit parts, and V5 answers about one and a half. The 2031 range needs a dollar projection and a stated confidence level; Caplet has a formula and the false phrase "cannot miss". The case's growth cues ("entrepreneurial mindset and passion for innovation", "Laura ultimately chooses") are under-read, so the roughly 9% stock share is never explained in client terms. The fundraising draft has no current prep: the only file is stale, contradicts V5's cap, and suggests matching, which the team's own research says not to do. None of the 11 filled WInS notes mentions flexibility, liquidity or the residency, so the TNA reflections must carry the client link. New insights a top team would use: the fixed $50k loses about 20% of its buying power from 2033 to 2042, and the case hands that gap to co-sponsors ("early operations"); Laura's total commitment of about $645-675k exceeds her $450k of deposits (MODEL); 2031 is the start of a two-year campaign; co-sponsors may judge a US-dollar promise in NT$. The kit also contains a case violation: D6 says Laura "adds her own money" for payments.

The kit's reason is a pre-set test (keep 10% of the gift in 95% of paths) that its own memo calls a value judgement. The 15 Oct brief asked for a principle, but none has been chosen.
